cloudflared Output Drives Tunnel Card State

nodes.label: Cloudfairy Watcher Panel (output -> card state)
nodes.rationale: Maps cloudflared output to UI: URL -> link with Copy/Open/QR, 'Registered tunnel connection' -> Live, ERR -> readable error, closed port -> warning until server starts.

nodes.label: Line-by-Line Output Parsing
nodes.rationale: Tunnel state is derived from cloudflared stdout/stderr: banner URL -> publicUrl, 'Registered tunnel connection' -> running, 'ERR' -> error; child exit polling -> stopped/error.

nodes.label: In-App Self Update
nodes.rationale: Offers to install new versions on launch then restarts; only signed updates from GitHub Releases are accepted.

nodes.label: OS Code Signing (Apple Notarization, Windows SmartScreen)
nodes.norm_label: os code signing (apple notarization, windows smartscreen)

nodes.label: CI and Releases (GitHub Actions)
nodes.rationale: Tauri cannot cross-compile installers, so CI builds each OS natively; version tags create draft releases.

nodes.label: Dark Theme Design
nodes.rationale: Near-black surfaces with subtle borders, orange-to-pink gradient accent, and green/amber/grey semantic status colors.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
nodes.rationale: The app exposes localhost ports via cloudflared quick tunnels yielding random *.trycloudflare.com URLs.

nodes.label: Cloudfairy Dark Mode Screenshot
nodes.rationale: README hero screenshot showing the single-window app in dark theme with three tunnels in different lifecycle states (live, starting, stopped) so readers see every state at once.

nodes.label: cloudflared Version Status Pill
nodes.rationale: Green dot indicates cloudflared binary is detected and ready; ties to the app's cloudflared update-check feature.

nodes.label: Create Tunnel Form
nodes.rationale: Minimal inputs: local port or address (accepts bare port like 3000 or host:port) and optional name, plus a gradient orange primary 'Create tunnel' button; low-friction quick tunnel creation.

nodes.label: App Header (Logo + cloudflared Version Badge + Settings)
nodes.norm_label: app header (logo + cloudflared version badge + settings)
nodes.rationale: Top bar with orange cloud logo, a green-dot pill showing the installed cloudflared version (2026.10.7), and a gear icon for settings; surfaces binary health at a glance.

nodes.label: Local Server Not Responding Warning
nodes.rationale: Amber banner explaining nothing is answering on the local port so the public URL will error until the server runs; proactive, plain-language guidance.

nodes.label: Collapsible Logs + Edit/Remove Actions
nodes.rationale: Logs hidden by default behind a chevron to keep cards compact; Edit is disabled while a tunnel runs, enabled when stopped.

nodes.label: Public trycloudflare.com URL Panel
nodes.rationale: Shows the generated quick-tunnel URL in monospace with copy, open-in-browser and QR code buttons; placeholder text when starting or stopped.

nodes.label: Start/Stop Tunnel Control
nodes.rationale: Neutral Stop button for running tunnels, accent-colored Start button for stopped ones, so the primary action is visually emphasized.

nodes.label: Tunnel Status Indicator (Live / Getting a URL / Stopped)
nodes.norm_label: tunnel status indicator (live / getting a url / stopped)
nodes.rationale: Color-coded dot plus text: green Live with uptime and connection count, amber 'Getting a URL...', grey Stopped; conveys tunnel lifecycle state.

nodes.label: Tunnel Card
nodes.rationale: Each tunnel is a card with name, local URL in monospace, status indicator, Start/Stop toggle, URL panel, collapsible Logs, and Edit/Remove actions; the live card gets a green border to stand out.

nodes.label: Light Theme Visual Style
nodes.rationale: Warm off-white background, white rounded cards, orange-to-pink gradient accent for primary actions, semantic green/amber/gray status colors; a light-mode counterpart to a dark-mode screenshot.

nodes.label: Cloudfairy Light Mode Screenshot
nodes.rationale: README hero screenshot showing the single-window app with three example tunnels in different states (Live, Getting a URL, Stopped) so readers see the whole tunnel lifecycle at a glance.

nodes.label: cloudflared Version Status Pill
nodes.rationale: Green dot plus 'cloudflared 2026.10.7' confirms the bundled/installed cloudflared binary is available and shows its version (ties to the cloudflared update check).

nodes.label: Create Tunnel Form
nodes.rationale: Minimal input: 'Local port or address' (accepts bare port like 3000 or host:port like localhost:5173), optional Name, and a gradient orange 'Create tunnel' primary button; designed for one-step quick tunnel creation.

nodes.label: App Header (logo, cloudflared status, settings)
nodes.rationale: Top bar with orange cloud logo and 'Cloudfairy' wordmark on the left, binary status and settings on the right; keeps global state separate from per-tunnel cards.

nodes.label: Local Server Not Answering Warning
nodes.rationale: Amber banner explaining that nothing answers on localhost:8080 so the public URL will show an error page until the local server runs; plain-language guidance instead of raw errors.

nodes.label: Collapsible Logs Toggle
nodes.rationale: Per-tunnel cloudflared logs hidden behind a chevron disclosure to keep cards compact.

nodes.label: Public trycloudflare URL Bar
nodes.rationale: Shows the generated *.trycloudflare.com quick-tunnel URL with copy, open-in-browser and QR code icon buttons; falls back to placeholder text ('Asking Cloudflare for a public URL...', 'Start the tunnel to get a public URL.') in other states.

nodes.label: Tunnel Actions (Start/Stop, Edit, Remove)
nodes.rationale: Stop is a neutral outlined button while running; Start uses the orange gradient primary style when stopped. Edit is greyed out while a tunnel runs and enabled only when stopped.

nodes.label: Tunnel Card
nodes.rationale: One card per tunnel (examples: Storefront :3000, Docs site :8080, API :8000) with name, local URL in monospace, status, public URL area and footer actions; the live card gets a green border to stand out.

nodes.label: Tunnel Status Indicator (Live / Getting a URL / Stopped)
nodes.norm_label: tunnel status indicator (live / getting a url / stopped)
nodes.rationale: Color-coded dot and text: green 'Live · 12m 36s · 4 connections' shows uptime and connection count, amber 'Getting a URL...' while waiting on Cloudflare, gray 'Stopped' when idle.

nodes.label: cloudflared tunnel --no-autoupdate --url <target>
nodes.rationale: cloudflared only makes outbound connections, so no router/firewall ports need opening.

nodes.label: Outbound Connection, No Open Ports or Account
nodes.norm_label: outbound connection, no open ports or account

nodes.label: Cloudfairy
nodes.rationale: Desktop GUI so users don't run cloudflared in a terminal and copy the URL from its logs; no Cloudflare account or domain needed.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
nodes.rationale: Quick tunnels need no account/domain but have no uptime guarantee and a new URL each start, so they suit testing and sharing, not production.

nodes.label: Protocol Setting (Auto / QUIC / HTTP2)
nodes.rationale: HTTP2 is offered for networks that block UDP, which QUIC needs.

nodes.label: 429 Too Many Requests (Quick Tunnel Rate Limit)
nodes.norm_label: 429 too many requests (quick tunnel rate limit)

nodes.label: SEO, Open Graph and Twitter Meta Tags
nodes.norm_label: seo, open graph and twitter meta tags

nodes.label: Settings Dialog (#settings-dialog)
nodes.rationale: Changes apply only to tunnels started after saving.

nodes.label: Page Not Found (404)
nodes.rationale: noindex so the error page is excluded from search; links back to /cloudfairy/ since the site is served under the GitHub Pages project path.

nodes.label: Hero: Share localhost in One Click
nodes.norm_label: hero: share localhost in one click

nodes.label: README Hero Banner
nodes.rationale: Shows the core transformation localhost:3000 -> cloudflared -> trycloudflare.com URL marked Live, on the app's dark surface.

nodes.label: Open Graph Social Card
nodes.rationale: 1280x640 share image: 'Share localhost with a public link in one click' plus localhost:3000 -> trycloudflare.com pill.

nodes.label: Cloudfairy App Icon
nodes.rationale: Rounded gradient square with white cloud, sparkles and a forward arrow (localhost going out).

nodes.label: Find or Download cloudflared
nodes.rationale: Search order: Settings path, then the managed downloaded copy, then PATH and usual install locations (Homebrew, winget, Program Files); one click downloads the official release if missing.

nodes.label: Copy / Open in Browser / QR Code
nodes.norm_label: copy / open in browser / qr code

nodes.label: Update Signing (TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY)
nodes.rationale: The updater only installs files signed with the private key; if the key is lost installed copies can no longer update, so keep a backup.

nodes.label: Cloudfairy App Icon
nodes.rationale: Rounded-square orange-to-pink gradient with a white cloud containing a pink right arrow and two sparkles; represents tunneling local traffic to the cloud.

nodes.label: Subtitle: Free desktop app for Cloudflare quick tunnels (Windows, macOS, Linux)
nodes.norm_label: subtitle: free desktop app for cloudflare quick tunnels (windows, macos, linux)

nodes.label: Tagline: Share localhost with a public link in one click
nodes.norm_label: tagline: share localhost with a public link in one click

nodes.label: Tunnel Illustration: localhost:3000 to trycloudflare.com URL
nodes.norm_label: tunnel illustration: localhost:3000 to trycloudflare.com url

nodes.label: Social Share Card (og-image)
nodes.rationale: 1280x640 dark-themed Open Graph card with app icon, wordmark, headline, platform subtitle, and a localhost-to-trycloudflare tunnel illustration.

nodes.label: Tunnels Saved Between Launches
nodes.rationale: Tunnels are remembered but never auto-started, and every cloudflared process is stopped on quit.
